fatal_errors: The cited evidence does not establish that 0.5–2 at.% Si in equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can produce a continuous external SiO2-rich scale rather than internal oxidation or brittle silicides.
The proposed bulk Si addition does not reconstruct the demonstrated silicide-coating intervention or its self-healing mixed-oxide mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis directly addresses oxidation resistance while imposing mechanical-property constraints and supplies useful exposure limits, controls, microscopy, thermogravimetry, phase analysis, and mechanical tests. It is therefore testable as an alternative. However, it differs substantially from the target intervention, which uses a silicide coating on processed HfNbTaTiZr and derives protection from self-healing Zr/Hf-rich oxide filling. The generated mechanism instead assumes that a very dilute bulk Si addition will sustain a continuous SiO2-rich barrier, a claim not demonstrated by the cited studies and thermodynamically questionable in an alloy rich in highly oxygen-reactive Hf, Zr, and Ti. E1 only gives generic evidence that Al/Cr/Si additions may improve RHEA oxidation while also warning of brittle intermetallics; E2–E4 do not validate the proposed intervention in this composition. The predicted oxidation improvement and retained mechanics align qualitatively with the objective, but no quantitative oxidation-rate target is given, and the falsification threshold of greater than 20% mechanical degradation is inconsistent with the prediction of retention within 10%, leaving an ambiguous 10–20% range.
